organization.name: Security Alliance (SEAL)
organization.summary: Nonprofit that shares crypto threat intelligence and security standards. Its website footer names Open Security Alliance, a 501(c)(3). The GitHub organization security-alliance was created 2023-08-04 and has 47 public repositories. SEAL describes itself as a crypto ISAC with SEAL 911, SEAL Intel, SEAL Frameworks and SEAL Certifications, plus Safe Harbor, Wargames and lazarus.group. The proposals name Dickson Wu, Matta and Sara as project leads. Public team size: Not found in public sources.

claims.claim: A public preview covers the 20 largest Ethereum DeFi protocols.
claims.method: The preview page returns HTTP 200 and its embedded data lists 20 protocol slugs (Lido, Aave, SSV Network, Spark, LayerZero, Ethena, Morpho, Maker, Uniswap, Chainlink and others). Whether they are the 20 largest by TVL was not checked.

claims.claim: The prototype maps contracts and proxies, collects audits with stated commit and scope, rebuilds audited code and compares it to live bytecode.
claims.method: The page presents per-contract results with audit report links and describes its method and limits. No repository or tooling is linked, so the comparison was not reproduced. The page calls itself an early prototype with results that are incomplete and some wrong.

claims.claim: 92 of 157 protocols on the Rekt list were hacked through unaudited or out-of-scope code (Ackee, 2023).

sources.label: Ackee article, link in the proposal

claims.method: The archived copy, dated 2023-09-19 and written by Josef Gattermayer, states 92 out of 157 protocols listed on Rekt. The live article URL returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-28, so the archived copy was used.
SEAL's own page states 3,300+ tickets handled. The count is self-reported and no independent record was found. The seal-911 repository is public and was last pushed 2026-11-22.

claims.claim: The register will cover every Ethereum DeFi protocol over USD 1 million TVL, refreshed monthly.
claims.method: This is a future commitment. The preview covers 20 protocols and says it is a single snapshot. No monthly refresh could be observed yet.

claims.claim: The dataset will be published under CC BY 4.0.
claims.method: A future commitment. No dataset repository or license file for the register was found.
